_comment: ADR-0717 S5 kernel-source mutation kill table. Each entry disables ONE guard in the trusted kernel (crates/axeyum-lean-kernel/src/{tc,inductive,quotient}.rs) and records whether the kernel_differential corpus (32 cases, run against pinned Lean 4.30.0) detected it. Measured by hand on 2026-08-30 in lane l0-s5-kernel-differential's isolated worktree via a one-off runner (never committed; mutating tracked source in a shared checkout breaks other lanes' builds, so this is not a script other lanes can run unattended -- re-measuring requires manually reapplying each `old`/`new` snippet pair below, one at a time, against a clean tree, then reverting). This artifact is the ledger of that measurement, not an automatically re-derivable one; scripts/check-kernel-differential-mutants.py checks the artifact's own internal consistency (every subsystem present, every status one of KILLED/SURVIVED, every KILLED entry names at least one flipped case) rather than re-running cargo, which would need ~8 kernel rebuilds and is a job for a human-triggered re-measurement, not a CI gate.

baseline.note: the unmutated kernel_differential_corpus_matches_pinned_lean run, confirmed passing before and after every mutation below

mutants.guard: the level_is_zero(l) restriction that confines proof irrelevance to Sort 0 (Prop)
mutants.mutation: always return Some(ty) regardless of the sort's level, so proof irrelevance applies to Type as well as Prop
mutants.note: 10 of 32 cases flipped, all to P0. This is the corpus's single most valuable kill: proof_irrelevance::type_is_not_irrelevant_negative is precisely the case this mutation targets, but the mutation is so unsound it also breaks nine unrelated negative controls across five other subsystems, because 'two distinct closed Type-sorted terms are not defeq' is load-bearing everywhere a mismatch case relies on def_eq distinguishing them.

mutants.guard: the undeclared_universe_param closure check on a declaration's type/value
mutants.mutation: skip the check entirely (drop the Err branch, keep the param unused)
mutants.note: Exactly the targeted case flips, and only that one -- the cleanest kill in the table.

mutants.guard: the non-positive-occurrence rejection when the family occurs in a Pi domain
mutants.mutation: gate the Err branch behind `false &&`, disabling it
mutants.note: inductives::non_positive_occurrence_negative did NOT flip. Not yet root-caused: either this specific occurrence check is not the one the corpus's `Bad.mk : (Bad -> Codomain) -> Bad` construction actually reaches (a different positivity check elsewhere in the group-admission path may reject it first), or admission fails earlier for an unrelated structural reason that also happens to reject this term. This is an honest gap: the corpus does not currently prove THIS guard is load-bearing for that case, and the true mechanism needs a follow-up bisection (e.g. tracing which KernelError variant actually fires under the mutation with an added eprintln) that this lane did not have time to complete.

mutants.mutation: always take `rec_rules.first()`, ignoring the major's actual constructor tag
mutants.note: This mutation is caught before ANY of the 32 differential cases print, almost certainly because build_logic_prelude's own internal proofs (Or.elim, Iff.mp, etc.) use recursors with multiple rules and the wrong-rule substitution produces an ill-typed intermediate that panics deep in the prelude build. A strong, unambiguous signal that the wrong-rule mutation is caught -- just not attributable to one differential case, since the corpus never got the chance to run.

projections::out_of_range_index_negative did NOT flip -- Axeyum still rejects it. Read together with infer_projection's own field-walking loop (crates/axeyum-lean-kernel/src/tc.rs, the `for previous_index in 0..field_index` loop a few lines below this guard): once the explicit bounds check is gone, walking past the last real field still runs out of Pi binders in the constructor's telescope and hits the loop's own `else { return Err(MalformedProjectionConstructor) }`. So this specific guard is REDUNDANT with a second, structural one for THIS case shape -- a real, positive finding (defense in depth), not a blind spot, though it does mean this differential case cannot distinguish the two guards from each other.

mutants.guard: the inductive_ok && zero_ok && succ_ok shape validation of the declared `Nat`
mutants.mutation: gate the Err branch behind `false &&`, disabling it
mutants.note: Expected to survive: every literals case in this corpus uses build_logic_prelude's own correctly-shaped Nat, so none of the four cases ever exercises the bootstrap validator's failure path. This is a genuine, named coverage gap -- see the report's honesty statement -- not a surprise.

mutants.guard: the is_named_quotient_member(constructor_name, "mk") check on the major's head constructor
mutants.mutation: drop that sub-check, keeping only the arity/kind checks
mutants.note: Expected to survive: this corpus builds exactly one quotient package per kernel instance, so there is never a second, non-canonical 'mk'-shaped constructor for a wrong one to be confused with. Another named coverage gap, not a surprise.

mutants.guard: the per-argument `check_core(argument, domain, ctx)` loop against each Pi's domain
mutants.mutation: skip the loop body, keeping the arguments unused
mutants.note: Neither conversion case itself flips (their mismatch is caught by a SEPARATE declared-type-vs-inferred-type def_eq check at Theorem admission, not by infer_app's per-argument loop), but two OTHER subsystems' cases -- both built via a bare `kernel.infer(...)` on a raw malformed application -- flip to P0. This is the clearest evidence in the table that 'one guard, one subsystem' is not how this kernel's checks are actually organized: the same core argument-checking loop is load-bearing for recursor-application shape and quotient-primitive misuse, not for the conversion cases it was nominally assigned to.
